newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: KLASCO'S Q1 NET PROFIT RISES.
newsitem.headline: KLASCO'S Q1 NET PROFIT RISES.

text.p: Lithuania's state-run Klaipedos Stevedoring company (KLASCO) said on Thursday that its Q1 net profit advanced to 8.4 million litas compared to 4.5 million litas for the same period last year.

"Our net profit during the first three months of this year rose to 8.4 million litas compared to 4.5 million litas in the first quarter last year," the company's director of commerce, Egidijus Dagilis, told Reuters.
He also said that the company's income in the first quarter of 1997 rose to 52.3 million litas compared to 37.6 million litas in the same period last year.

"Our profit in the second quarter of the year might fall slightly as the amount of metal cargo passing through the port is declining," Dagilis added. KLASCO is the biggest stevedoring company in Lithuania.
The company said earlier that it reloaded 2.29 million tons of cargo in the first quarter of 1997.
The state has a 90 percent stake in the company which has 128.99 million litas in share capital.
The government earlier this month decided to double the share capital of the company from its reserves and the final decision is expected to be made at the shareholders' meeting scheduled for Monday.
The government has slated KLASCO for privatisation and the tender to draw up a privatisation plan for the company is expected to be announced soon.
